side_effects: Launches the Claude Code CLI as a child process via StdioProcess with the configured argv, working directory and environment
Runs `<executable> --help` (Shell.run, timeout 20) once per executable path to probe for --system-prompt-snapshot and --forward-subagent-text
handshake(...) launches a second, bare CLI process with --no-session-persistence and terminates it; a 20-second watchdog Task terminates it if the initialize never answers
Writes stream-json control_request / control_response / user messages to the child's stdin
Sets environment variable CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS when hydra.maxHeads is set
Records token spend into the global TokenLedger.shared on each result that carries usage
Terminates the child process on stop() and via the handshake watchdog
Spawns a detached Task from resolveApproval to send set_permission_mode after ExitPlanMode is approved
platform_assumptions: Swift concurrency with @MainActor isolation for the whole session class
Foundation URL/UUID/Date; Date(timeIntervalSince1970:) for rate limit reset times
Unix-style child process with stdin/stdout stream-json and a stderr tail (StdioProcess), as used on macOS
The Claude Code CLI binary is resolvable at configuration.executable and supports the stream-json control protocol
String.localizedCaseInsensitiveContains for tool result decline detection
persisted_fields: Session id: configuration.resumeID, else UUID().uuidString.lowercased(), passed as --session-id and returned from start()
No UserDefaults/@AppStorage in this file; the only cross-launch state is the CLI's own session store reached via --resume / --resume-session-at
ui_elements: Approval for ExitPlanMode: title "Implement this plan", options "Implement plan" (id allow, role .approve) and "Keep planning" (id deny, role .decline), kind .plan

Generic tool approval options: "Approve" (id allow, role .approve), "Approve for session" (id always, role .approveAlways, only when permission_suggestions is a non-empty array), "Decline" (id deny, role .decline)
Notice text "Context compacted." (level .info) on system subtype compact_boundary
Notice text "Claude hit a usage limit." plus " It resets at <UsageLimitSignal.format(date)>." when a reset time is known (level .warning)
Deny message on interrupt: "The user stopped the turn."
Deny message for ExitPlanMode: "The user wants to keep planning. Wait for their feedback before changing anything."
Deny message for other tools: "The user declined this action."

Error strings: "Claude could not load its commands.", "Claude's command discovery did not finish. Try again.", "Claude rejected the request.", "Claude exited.", "Claude stopped before finishing.", "Droppy Code does not support this request."

Default tool titles: "Shell command", "Read file", "Write file", "Edit file", "Edit notebook", "Find files", "Search", "List files", "Fetch page", "Search the web", "Subagent", and "Tool" as the approval fallback name
Skill tool title format "Skill · <skill or command>"; MCP tool title format "<server> · <tool>" split on "__" with fallback server name "MCP"
ModelOption fastTier string "fast" when supportsFastMode is true
feature_notes: Base argv: -p, --input-format stream-json, --output-format stream-json, --verbose, --include-partial-messages, --permission-prompt-tool stdio, --setting-sources user,project,local, --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, --permission-mode <mode>
--model is only added when configuration.model is non-nil and != "default"; --effort <effort> when non-empty; --settings {"fastMode":true} when fastMode
--mcp-config <path> --strict-mcp-config only when MCPProviderConfig.claudeConfigPath() is non-nil, so with no connected servers Claude reads its own config
--system-prompt-snapshot off is appended whenever `--help` advertises that option, including for resumed chats

Hydra native: --agents <HydraPrompts.claudeAgents(hydra).compactString>, --forward-subagent-text when supported, env CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS = maxHeads; Hydra fallback (heads on another provider): --disallowedTools Agent Task plus HydraPrompts.fallbackPolicy
Exactly one --append-system-prompt per session, joining the Hydra policy (or nothing) and AntiSlopPolicy.instructions(enabled:) with "\n\n"
Resume path: --resume <resumeID> plus --resume-session-at <anchor> when resumeAt is set; otherwise --session-id <id>
Initialize control request payload: {"subtype":"initialize","hooks":null}; with native Hydra it also carries agentProgressSummaries: true and forwardSubagentText: true
Models parsed from initialization "models" array fields: value, displayName, description, supportedEffortLevels, supportsFastMode; isDefault when value == "default"

handshake() argv omits --include-partial-messages and adds --no-session-persistence; it sends request_id "handshake" and only accepts a control_response whose response.request_id == "handshake"; 20-second watchdog terminate

send(): set_permission_mode control request when the computed mode changed, set_model (model null when "default") when the model changed, then a user message whose content is image blocks {type:image, source:{type:base64, media_type, data}} followed by one {type:text, text} block

interrupt(): only when turnActive; denies every pending tool with {behavior:deny, message:"The user stopped the turn.", interrupt:true}, emits requestResolved for each, then sends the interrupt control request
compact() writes the literal user message "/compact"

resolveApproval allow/always -> {behavior:allow, updatedInput:<original input>}; "always" also sets updatedPermissions to the permission_suggestions with each entry's "destination" forced to "session"
Approving ExitPlanMode emits .modeChanged(.build) and switches the CLI permission mode accordingly
answerQuestion joins each question's selected values with ", " into input.answers and replies {behavior:allow, updatedInput:...}
stopAgent looks up tasksByAgent and sends {subtype:"stop_task", task_id:<id>}; returns false when the agent is unknown
Message routing by top-level "type": control_response, control_request, control_cancel_request, system, stream_event, assistant, user, result, rate_limit_event
rate_limit_event handled only when rate_limit_info.status == "rejected"; reset time read from resetsAt or resetsAtSeconds as Unix seconds
system subtypes handled: init (adopts a new session_id and emits sessionReady), compact_boundary, task_started, task_progress, task_notification
task_progress maps usage.total_tokens -> tokens and usage.tool_uses -> toolCalls, plus summary and last_tool_name
task_notification status mapping: "failed" -> .failed, "stopped" -> .interrupted, anything else -> .completed; the head's stream state is cleared there

task_started is ignored when skip_transcript is true or when neither subagent_type nor task_type == "local_agent" is present (background shell tasks pass through); agent id is tool_use_id when present, else task_id
Streaming block ids are "<messageID>-<index>"; content_block types handled are text, thinking and tool_use; deltas handled are text_delta and thinking_delta

Assistant messages whose message.model == "<synthetic>" are not shown as model text; only when isApiErrorMessage is true and the text is not one of "No response requested." / "(no content)" is it emitted as a warning notice
TodoWrite input is converted to a TodoStep list with status mapping completed -> .done, in_progress -> .active, default -> .pending

Tool results: names in hiddenResultTools (AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, EnterPlanMode, TodoWrite, ToolSearch) are skipped; an is_error result whose text contains "declined" or "doesn't want" (case-insensitive) becomes .declined instead of .failed
A result arriving before isStarted is treated as a launch failure and its errors become launchError, thrown by start() via didClose
turnSpend sums input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + output_tokens, over usage.iterations when present
contextUsage uses the last iteration (or usage itself), the same four token fields, and the max modelUsage[*].contextWindow as the window; nil when used == 0
On a result, main stream state and toolNames are cleared but agentStreams are deliberately kept so background heads keep streaming
A failing result whose text matches UsageLimitSignal emits .usageLimit even without a preceding rate_limit_event
can_use_tool is the only supported inbound control_request; anything else is answered with a control_response error
AskUserQuestion maps questions[].question/header/options[].label/description/multiSelect into QuestionRequest with allowsOther: true and isSecret: false; the question id is the prompt text itself

Approval kind mapping: ToolCall .command -> .command, .edit -> .fileChange, everything else -> .tool; command approvals show request.description as detail, others show the call's own detail; request.decision_reason becomes reason
modeName: interaction .plan always yields "plan"; otherwise supervised -> "default", autoAcceptEdits -> "acceptEdits", auto -> "auto", fullAccess -> "bypassPermissions"

toolCall returns nil for TodoWrite, AskUserQuestion, ExitPlanMode, EnterPlanMode, ToolSearch; BashOutput, KillShell, KillBash, Monitor, TaskOutput and TaskStop render as .command with the bare tool name as title
Edits are only built when withEdits is true (approval cards pass false and build diffs later from the assistant message)

didClose resumes every pending control continuation with ProviderError.failed(launchError ?? stderr tail ?? "Claude exited."), resolves pending tool requests, and only emits .exited when the session had started and stop() was not called

Runs `<claude executable> auth status` (Shell.run, 20-second timeout) to make the CLI refresh its OAuth token
HTTPS GET to https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage with a 15-second request timeout, carrying the account's bearer token
Launches a short-lived Claude Code CLI process (stream-json) for the get_usage control request, with a 20-second watchdog that terminates it, and terminates it on exit
Delegates to other providers' readers which have their own process/network effects
platform_assumptions: macOS Keychain accessed through the /usr/bin/security command-line tool, including the hex-encoded output form that `security -w` produces for binary items
Unix home directory layout with a ~/.claude directory (NSString appendingPathComponent)
@MainActor isolation with nonisolated helpers for pure parsing
persisted_fields: Read from .credentials.json / Keychain JSON: claudeAiOauth.accessToken (String), claudeAiOauth.expiresAt (Double, milliseconds since epoch, divided by 1000), claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType (String), claudeAiOauth.rateLimitTier (String)
Environment keys consulted: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, USER, LOGNAME

Usage JSON fields parsed: limits[].percent, limits[].kind, limits[].group, limits[].scope.model.display_name, limits[].resets_at, five_hour.utilization, five_hour.resets_at, seven_day.utilization, seven_day.resets_at, extra_usage.is_enabled, extra_usage.utilization; the CLI path adds rate_limits and subscription_type
ui_elements: Window titles from windowTitle(minutes:): "Usage limit" (nil), 300 -> "5-hour limit", 1440 -> "Daily", 10080 -> "Weekly", 40320...44640 -> "Monthly", other multiples of 1440 -> "<n>-day limit", else "<max(1, minutes/60)>-hour limit"

Claude window titles: kind "session" -> "5-hour limit", kind "weekly_all" -> "Weekly · all models", otherwise "<Group> · <model display name>" or just the capitalized group (default group "Usage"); fallback windows "5-hour limit" and "Weekly · all models"; extra usage window titled "Extra usage"
titlePrefix option renders "<Prefix> · <base title>" and prefixes ids with the lowercased prefix plus "-"

Codex plan names: pro -> "Pro 20x", prolite / "pro lite" -> "Pro 5x", ent26 / hc -> "Enterprise", self_serve_business_prolite -> "Business Premium", self_serve_business_usage_based -> "Business", enterprise_cbp_automation -> "Enterprise (Automation)", enterprise_cbp_usage_based -> "Enterprise", education -> "Edu", edu_plus -> "Edu Plus", edu_pro -> "Edu Pro", otherwise the capitalized raw value
ResetOutcome messages: "Usage was reset.", "There was no active usage to reset.", "No banked resets are left.", "That reset was already used."
ResetCreditError descriptions: "Codex CLI not found.", "Codex returned an unknown reset result.", and the rejected message verbatim
feature_notes: exposesLimits is true only for codex, claude, antigravity, copilot, commandcode, zai and pi; cursor, opencode, grok, deepseek, meta and devin return nil from read()
zai is the only provider served by the apiKey overload of read(_:apiKey:); through an executable it returns nil
Claude read order: OAuth usage endpoint first, CLI get_usage only if that yields nothing
A stored token expiring within the next 300 seconds triggers `claude auth status` and a re-read of the credentials before the request
On HTTP 401 or 403 the login is refreshed once and retried, and only if the re-read access token actually differs from the previous one
Only HTTP 200 with parseable JSON is accepted; the windows come from json.limits with json itself as the root for the fallback fields
Credentials lookup order: $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/.credentials.json, then ~/.claude/.credentials.json, then Keychain with -a $USER (or $LOGNAME), then Keychain without an account
Keychain output starting with "{" is used as-is; otherwise an even-length all-hex string is hex-decoded to bytes before JSON parsing
ClaudeLogin.planName capitalizes subscriptionType and appends the first \d+x match from rateLimitTier in parentheses, e.g. "max" + "default_claude_max_20x" -> "Max (20x)"
Usage request headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, anthropic-beta: oauth-2025-04-20, Accept: application/json, timeoutInterval 15

CLI fallback launches `-p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --verbose` in the system temporary directory, sends request_id "droppy-code-init" with {"subtype":"initialize","hooks":null}, then on its response sends request_id "droppy-code-usage" with {"subtype":"get_usage"}
The CLI usage response is read from response.response.rate_limits (and its own "limits" array) with the plan name from response.response.subscription_type

parseClaudeUsage skips limit rows with no numeric percent; window ids are "<idPrefix><kind>-<index>", fallback ids "<idPrefix>five_hour" / "<idPrefix>seven_day", extra usage id "<idPrefix>extra-usage"
The five_hour/seven_day fallback is only consulted when the limits array produced no windows at all; extra usage is appended regardless, but only when extra_usage.is_enabled is true
parseClaudeUsage returns nil when no windows were produced, so the caller falls through to the next source
parseDate strips any fractional-second group matching \.\d+ before ISO8601 parsing, because Claude writes microsecond timestamps the ISO 8601 parser rejects

PlanLimits.problem exists so an expired login can be shown in the provider's own words instead of stale bars; resetCredits is documented as Codex-only and may hold fewer credits than availableCount when only a total was reported

files.purpose: A small provider-agnostic namespace that recognizes a usage-limit refusal in an error message, extracts the reset time it carries (Unix timestamp after a pipe, or a clock time with optional timezone), and formats a reset Date as friendly user-facing text.
key_symbols: static func matches(_ text: String) -> Bool
static func resetTime(in text: String, now: Date = .now) -> Date?
static func format(_ date: Date) -> String
calls_into: Used by ClaudeSession.handleResult and its rate_limit_event handling in the same bundle
state_owned: None: a stateless enum namespace with only static functions
side_effects: None: pure text and date computation, no I/O
platform_assumptions: Foundation/ICU date formatting with the user's current Calendar and locale (formatted(date: .omitted, time: .shortened) produces the locale's short time)
NSRegularExpression-backed String range matching including the (?i) inline flag
Calendar.current for today/tomorrow checks, so results depend on the device's time zone unless the text named one
ui_elements: format() output shapes: the short time alone for today (for example "3:31 PM"), "tomorrow at <time>", "<Weekday> at <time>" (for example "Thursday at 9:00 AM") within the next 6 days, otherwise abbreviated date plus short time
feature_notes: matches() lowercases the text and returns true on any of: "usage limit", "hit your limit", "usage_limit", "limit reached", "out of extra usage"
Timestamp form: regex \|\s*(\d{9,}) (at least 9 digits after a pipe), as in "usage limit reached|1757865600"; values greater than 1e11 are treated as milliseconds and divided by 1000
Clock form: regex (?i)resets?(?:\s+at)?\s+(\d{1,2})(?::(\d{2}))?\s*(am|pm), matching "resets 3pm" or "resets at 3:30 pm"
12-hour conversion: PM with hour < 12 adds 12; AM with hour == 12 becomes 0; missing minutes default to 0
A timezone in parentheses matching \(([A-Za-z_]+/[A-Za-z_]+)\) (for example "(America/New_York)") overrides Calendar.current.timeZone for the computed reset
The clock time is resolved as the next matching time strictly after `now` using Calendar.nextDate(after:matching:matchingPolicy:.nextTime)
The weekday branch of format() compares against a 6-day horizon computed from Date.now (not from the passed date), so a date more than 6 days out falls through to the abbreviated date form
resetTime returns nil when neither pattern matches, and also when the matched clock digits fail to parse as an hour
unresolved_questions: The `now` parameter defaults to .now but format() always uses Date.now for its 6-day horizon rather than an injectable reference, so the two are not consistently testable; whether tests rely on this is not determinable from this file
Which providers besides Claude feed text into matches() cannot be established from this file alone
